title: Signage development examples
slide_intent: Teach designers to choose what someone on the street should see first. A person looking for a door needs a venue name and a direction. A person discovering a show needs a title and an image.
strategic_value: The Graves Gallery mark and Sheffield Museums seal can connect an exhibition campaign to the venue that hosts it while allowing the two signs to answer different questions.
demonstration: Two photographs present signs on building exteriors. The green directional sign enlarges the venue name above a left arrow and facilities. The exhibition sign reduces the venue mark, gives Invisible Wounds a yellow title and devotes the right side to a woodland image.
practical_value: Choose the hierarchy for a physical sign by its job. Lead with the venue and direction for wayfinding, or give the exhibition title and artwork priority for a campaign.
